\chapter{Greetings People Actually Say}
\label{ch:te-greetings-people-say}
\hlchaptermodality{91}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can greet someone the way Telugu speakers greet each other day to day: are you well, long time, what's new, where to, have you eaten.}

Complete TE-R91-second-pass-greetings: everyday greetings and partings, from cold.

\section[bāgunnārā?]{\te{బాగున్నారా}? (bāgunnārā?) — are you well?}

\label{lesson:TE-C91-areyouwell}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for leave, then the Telugu for let's go.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{బాగున్నారా}?}
\textbf{\te{బాగున్నారా}?} (\emph{bāgunnārā?}) — \textquotedblleft{}are you well?\textquotedblright{}.

It is the answer you already give, \textbf{\te{బాగున్నాను}}, turned into a question: the respectful ending \textbf{-\te{ారు}} and the question mark \textbf{-\te{ఆ}} you know from \textbf{\te{అవునా}?}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The greeting most people open with, built from your own answer.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bāgunnārā?}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bāgunnārā?}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{bāgunnārā?}, then answer \emph{bāgunnānu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for leave, then the Telugu for let's go, then say \emph{bāgunnārā?} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{బాగున్నారా}? mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Are you well?\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[cālā rōjulaindi]{\te{చాలా} \te{రోజులైంది} (cālā rōjulaindi) — it has been a long time}

\label{lesson:TE-C91-longtime}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for let's go, then the Telugu for are you well.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{చాలా} \te{రోజులైంది}}
\textbf{\te{చాలా} \te{రోజులైంది}} (\emph{cālā rōjulaindi}) — \textquotedblleft{}it has been a long time\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}many days have become\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{చాలా}} and \textbf{\te{రోజు}} are both yours already; \textbf{-\te{లు}} makes the days plural.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The greeting for someone you have not seen in a while.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cālā rōjulaindi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cālā rōjulaindi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{cālā rōjulaindi!}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for let's go, then the Telugu for are you well, then say \emph{cālā rōjulaindi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{చాలా} \te{రోజులైంది} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}It has been a long time\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ēṇṭi saṅgati?]{\te{ఏంటి} \te{సంగతి}? (ēṇṭi saṅgati?) — what's new?}

\label{lesson:TE-C91-whatsnew}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for are you well, then the Telugu for it has been a long time.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{ఏంటి} \te{సంగతి}?}
\textbf{\te{ఏంటి} \te{సంగతి}?} (\emph{ēṇṭi saṅgati?}) — \textquotedblleft{}what's new?\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}what's the matter?\textquotedblright{}, but warm.

\textbf{\te{ఏంటి}} is the everyday spoken form of \textbf{\te{ఏమిటి}}. Use it with friends, not with a stranger.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A friendly opener, and the spoken shape of a word you learned formally.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ēṇṭi saṅgati?}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ēṇṭi saṅgati?}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask a friend \emph{ēṇṭi saṅgati?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for are you well, then the Telugu for it has been a long time, then say \emph{ēṇṭi saṅgati?} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{ఏంటి} \te{సంగతి}? mean? (\textquotedblleft{}What's new?\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ekkaḍiki?]{\te{ఎక్కడికి}? (ekkaḍiki?) — where to?}

\label{lesson:TE-C91-whereto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for it has been a long time, then the Telugu for what's new.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{ఎక్కడికి}?}
\textbf{\te{ఎక్కడికి}?} (\emph{ekkaḍiki?}) — \textquotedblleft{}where to?\textquotedblright{}.

It is \textbf{\te{ఎక్కడ}}, \textquotedblleft{}where\textquotedblright{}, with the \textbf{-\te{కి}} \textquotedblleft{}to\textquotedblright{} ending. Asked of a neighbour on the street it is a greeting, not a demand; \emph{\te{ఇంటికి}}, \textquotedblleft{}home\textquotedblright{}, is a full answer.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A street greeting, and its answer from the last chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ekkaḍiki?}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ekkaḍiki?}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{ekkaḍiki?}, then answer \emph{iṇṭiki}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for it has been a long time, then the Telugu for what's new, then say \emph{ekkaḍiki?} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{ఎక్కడికి}? mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Where to?\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bhōñcēśārā?]{\te{భోంచేశారా}? (bhōñcēśārā?) — have you eaten?}

\label{lesson:TE-C91-eaten}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for what's new, then the Telugu for where to.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{భోంచేశారా}?}
\textbf{\te{భోంచేశారా}?} (\emph{bhōñcēśārā?}) — \textquotedblleft{}have you eaten?\textquotedblright{}.

It is \textbf{\te{భోజనం} \te{చేశారా}?}, \textquotedblleft{}have you done the meal?\textquotedblright{}, worn short in speech. Asked around a mealtime it is a greeting and a kindness; \textbf{\te{ఆ}, \te{అయింది}} — \textquotedblleft{}yes, done\textquotedblright{} — is enough of an answer.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Five greetings people actually use, one of them about food.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhōñcēśārā?}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhōñcēśārā?}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{bhōñcēśārā?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for what's new, then the Telugu for where to, then say \emph{bhōñcēśārā?} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{భోంచేశారా}? mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Have you eaten?\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Hello and goodbye, the everyday way — a second pass}

\label{lesson:TE-R91-second-pass-greetings}



\begin{quote}
You meet a neighbour you have not seen in a long time, around lunch. Say three things.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: the ending -\te{కి}, \textquotedblleft{}to\textquotedblright{}}]
\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{word} & \textbf{built from} \\
\midrule
\textbf{\te{ఇంటికి}} & house + -\te{కి} \\
\textbf{\te{ఎక్కడికి}?} & where + -\te{కి} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

The same \textbf{-\te{కి}} as \textbf{\te{నాకు}}: a direction, to a place or to a person.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item ask a friend what's new, then ask where they are going
  \item answer that you are going home
  \item at the door, tell your host to take care and to come soon
  \item take your leave formally, then hurry your group along
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Are you well? (\textbf{\te{బాగున్నారా}?}) Long time? (\textbf{\te{చాలా} \te{రోజులైంది}}.) What's new? (\textbf{\te{ఏంటి} \te{సంగతి}?}) Where to? (\textbf{\te{ఎక్కడికి}?}) Have you eaten? (\textbf{\te{భోంచేశారా}?}) Take care? (\textbf{\te{జాగ్రత్త}}.) Soon? (\textbf{\te{త్వరగా}}.) Home? (\textbf{\te{ఇంటికి}}.) Leave? (\textbf{\te{సెలవు}}.) Let's go? (\textbf{\te{పదండి}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{After the name — a second pass}

\label{lesson:TE-R91-second-pass-people}



\begin{quote}
You have given your name. Ask the next two questions: the job, and the address.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: one frame, many questions}]
\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{ask about you} & \textbf{ask what happened to you} \\
\midrule
\textbf{\te{మీ} \te{ఉద్యోగం} \te{ఏమిటి}?} & \textbf{\te{మీకు} \te{పెళ్ళి} \te{అయిందా}?} \\
\textbf{\te{మీ} \te{చిరునామా} \te{ఏమిటి}?} & \textbf{\te{మీకు} \te{ఏ} \te{భాషలు} \te{వచ్చు}?} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

\textbf{\te{మీ}} asks about something of yours; \textbf{\te{మీకు}} asks what is so, or what came, to you. The children question is the right-hand kind: \textbf{\te{మీకు} \te{పిల్లలు} \te{ఉన్నారా}?}
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item say you know English and a little Telugu
  \item introduce your son and your daughter
  \item say he is a good person, and our relative
  \item a neighbour asks where to, and whether you have eaten; answer both
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Children? (\textbf{\te{పిల్లలు}}.) A boy, a girl? (\textbf{\te{అబ్బాయి}}, \textbf{\te{అమ్మాయి}}.) A person? (\textbf{\te{మనిషి}}.) A relative? (\textbf{\te{బంధువు}}.) A job? (\textbf{\te{ఉద్యోగం}}.) A language? (\textbf{\te{భాష}}.) English? (\textbf{\te{ఇంగ్లీషు}}.) A wedding? (\textbf{\te{పెళ్ళి}}.) An address? (\textbf{\te{చిరునామా}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
